🇲🇽🌎 <u>US OPENS DOOR TO REVIEWING MEXICO'S PENDING EXTRADITION REQUESTS</u>

Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Mexico's unanswered extradition petitions "should be reviewed, of course" — while admitting he had no details. Between 2018 and 2026, Mexico filed 269 extradition requests with Washington; 233 remain pending, including former Tamaulipas governor García Cabeza de Vaca, wanted for organized crime and money laundering.

Sheinbaum has asked for reciprocity: in eight years, not one of those 269 requests has been completed.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>STEPHEN MILLER: MEXICO'S JUSTICE AND POLITICAL SYSTEMS "DON'T WORK" BECAUSE OF CARTELS</u>

Trump's deputy chief of staff for policy claimed Mexican cartels "control the territory," and that is why "the judicial, political and legal systems" of Mexico do not function — putting the cartels "in exactly the same legal situation as ISIS or Al Qaeda," except they operate "a few meters" from the US border instead of thousands of miles away.

He said it at the Pentagon, alongside War Secretary Pete Hegseth, at a "Medal for the Defense of the Mexican Border" ceremony. The FTO designation doing exactly what it was built for.

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S EXPORTS SMASH RECORD: $72.5 BILLION IN JUNE</u>

Mexico exported a record $72.55 billion in June, up 34.4% year-on-year, closing the best first half in its history with $389.7 billion in foreign sales, INEGI reported Monday (El Economista). The trade surplus hit $4.09 billion in June and $9.86 billion for the semester — and even the auto sector, despite US tariffs, grew 7.6%. While Washington taxes its own consumers, Mexico sells more to the world than ever.

🇲🇽💧 <u>DISASTER-PROOF WATER FOR ACAPULCO, HOUSING RELIEF FOR MORELOS</u>

The federal government is rebuilding Acapulco's water system to survive the next hurricane: elevated and protected pumping stations, hillside tanks to supply working-class colonias by gravity, nine wastewater treatment plants and a containment wall on the Canal del Muerto. "The goal is that Acapulco keeps its water, and even if a natural phenomenon comes, it keeps functioning," Sheinbaum said. The same package restructures housing debts in Morelos. Reconstruction with memory — not the abandonment the hurricanes left behind.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>FEDERAL FORCES BUST LOS CHAPITOS CELL LEADER IN MAZATLÁN</u>

Mexican federal forces arrested Ricardo Ozuna Tirado, alias "El Tío," alleged financial operator and leader of a Los Chapitos cell in La Cruz de Elota, Sinaloa. Intelligence work by the Navy, SSPC, FGR and CNI led to two properties in Mazatlán, where five more suspects were detained — including a US citizen — along with $100,000 in cash and weapons. No foreign agents, no US boots on the ground: Mexican institutions dismantling the cartel's money networks themselves.

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>CDMX PUBLIC INVESTMENT UP 2.6X IN FIRST HALF OF 2026</u>

Mexico City spent 17.66 billion pesos on public investment in the first half of 2026 — 2.6 times the same period last year, finance secretary Juan Pablo de Botton reported. Public works jumped 88.4%, water spending rose 28% to 7.1 billion pesos, and welfare grew 23%. All while the city's public debt has fallen 8.4% since 2018. Investing more while owing less: republican austerity in practice.

🇲🇽📱 <u>SHEINBAUM SEEKS NATIONAL CONSENSUS TO SHIELD KIDS FROM SOCIAL MEDIA</u>

President Sheinbaum said Mexico could simply ban cellphones in schools — but she wants a national consensus instead, bringing in parents, teachers and the kids themselves, and warned that unchecked screen time is turning into a public health problem. Specialists at the mañanera showed how platform-driven dopamine overload hits the prefrontal cortex of minors. Sixteen states have already restricted phones in classrooms. Regulate Big Tech with science and consensus, not decree.
banner: SHEINBAUM: PROTECT KIDS FROM SOCIAL MEDIA

🇲🇽🏫 <u>MEXICO'S SEP: MILITARIZED SCHOOLS ARE NOT PERMITTED, PERIOD</u>

After the death of 13-year-old Dafne at a "militarized academy" summer camp in Tamaulipas, Education Secretary Mario Delgado ordered every state government to audit schools selling military-style basic education. "It's not that they're prohibited — it's that they're not permitted. Neither the SEP nor the Defense Ministry authorizes this type of education," he said. Tamaulipas already found five more such schools; their permits are now under review. Childhood is not boot camp. The 4T is drawing the line.
